en: The Sūtra of the Great Golden Peacock King Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha, One Scroll;
the translator’s name lost, now appended to the Qin Records.
Namo Buddha. Namo Dharma. Namo Saṃgha of Bhikṣus. Namo to the Seven Buddhas, the Truly and Fully Enlightened Ones.
Awakened One!
Homage to the Pratyekabuddhas; homage to all the Arhats;
homage to Maitreya and all other Bodhisattvas.

Homage to all those who have attained the stage of non-returning (anāgāmin); homage to those who have attained the stage of once-returning (sakṛdāgāmin); homage to those who have attained the stage of stream-entry (srotāpanna).
Homage to those in the world who are correctly directed toward the goal.
Having paid homage to that assembly, I now offer my prostrations.
I wish to proclaim the Mahāmāyūrīvidyārājñī Sūtra.
May there be the fulfillment of all wishes.
May you auspicious spirits and deities listen attentively!
Whether they dwell in the void, on the earth, or in the waters—
be they devas, nāgas, asuras, mahoragas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, or mahoragas.
yakṣas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, gandharvas, unmādas, cetas, apasmāras, utpātās, and so forth.
Listen to what I say:
there are ghosts who feed on exhaled breath,
ghosts who eat rock honey, and ghosts who eat blood.
The marrow-eating spirits, the flesh-eating spirits,
the fat-eating spirits, the fetus-eating spirits,
the life-force-eating spirits, and the strength-eating spirits.
The hair-eating ghosts, the flower-eating ghosts,
the sound-eating ghosts, the breath-eating ghosts,
the evil-minded ghosts, and the conspiracy-minded ghosts.
O spirits with harmful intent who delight in taking the lives of others, and all you ghosts and deities:
listen as I recite this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī Sūtra.
Now, I offer you incense, flowers, and food; receive them.
Those who harbor harmful, evil, or treacherous intentions to injure you,
yet come to consume this incense with a mind of compassion, a virtuous mind,
and faith in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha of bhikṣus— [may they be protected].
Listen to what I say:
there are fourteen rākṣasīs;
the first is named Kālī, and the second is named Kālakā.
The third is named Kumbhāṇḍa; the fourth, Śuklabhāṇḍa;
the fifth, Puṣpanetra; the sixth, Bījagrāha;
the seventh, Keśagrāha; and the eighth, Pītākara.
The ninth is named Hanging Down; the tenth is named Hanging Down Extremely;
the eleventh is named Watching for an Opportunity; the twelfth is named Messenger of Yama;
the thirteenth is named Rākṣasa of Yama; and the fourteenth is named Flesh-Eating Ghost.
May you accept these flowers, incense, food, and drink from me;
protect such-and-such a person and all their kinsmen,
and cause my mantra-words to be accomplished as desired and auspiciously.
At that time I heard:
Once the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a young bhikṣu in the park named Śrī.
Not long after he had gone forth, while he was bathing the monks and splitting firewood,
a black snake emerged from beneath a piece of strange wood and bit the monk’s toe.
He fell to the ground in a swoon, his eyes rolled back,
and he spat foam from his mouth. At that time,
the Elder Ānanda saw that the bhikṣu Śrī’s illness was extremely grave.
Having seen this, he was struck with terror and went to where the Buddha was.
Prostrating himself with his head at the ground,
he paid homage to the Buddha and addressed him, saying, "World-Honored One."
In this Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park at Śrāvastī,
there was a newly ordained bhikṣu named Śrī who bathed for the Saṃgha and split firewood.
Beneath a different tree, a black snake emerged and bit the monk’s right toe.
He fell to the ground in a swoon, his eyes rolled back and he vomited foam. How should this be treated?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
"You shall uphold this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra of the Tathāgata to protect and bring auspiciousness to the bhikṣu Śrī."
By performing the boundary-binding and the binding of mantras,
one ensures that poisons cannot cause harm,
blades and staves cannot be applied, and all calamities are entirely eliminated.
Whether it is caused by devas, caused by nāgas,
caused by mahoragas, caused by garuḍas,
caused by gandharvas, or caused by kiṃnaras.
It is the doing of mahoragas, the doing of yakṣas,
the doing of rākṣasas, the doing of pretas,
the doing of piśācas, and the doing of bhūtas.
The deeds of the kumbhāṇḍas, the deeds of the pūtanas,
the deeds of the black pūtanas, the deeds of the gandharvas,
the deeds of the ummaddas, and the deeds of the cetas.
That which is caused by Ābhmara, that which is caused by Uttaka,
that which is caused by Kiccha, that which is caused by Kammaṇa,
that which is caused by Khakkhuda, and that which is caused by Kīlana.
That which is done by Vitata, that which is done by Lipica,
and that which is done by Bhisaka;
it is an unlawful meal and an unlawful vomiting.
To view what is not Dharma as not Dharma and to raise it [as a charge];
to transgress what is not Dharma and to touch upon what is not Dharma;
or if there is a feverish illness lasting one or two days.
On the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, or seventh day;
in half a month, or a month;
arising once a day, or at every moment.
Whether it be fevers caused by spirits or ghosts, or afflictions arising from wind, fire, or water;
or choleraic heat;
or pain in half the body, headaches, or eye pains.
Pain in the face, pain in the jaw, pain in the throat, pain in the neck; pain in the ears,
pain in the teeth, pain in the mouth,
pain in the heart, and pain in the back.
Abdominal pain;
pain in the lower back, the genitals, and the thighs;
pain in the shoulders, hands, and feet.
May all pains in the limbs and joints be entirely eliminated and healed; may [this person] be protected. For such-and-so person, he recites this verse and incantation:
"Peaceful by day, peaceful by night, always peaceful in between; peaceful and secure day and night, protected by all Buddhas. Then he spoke the incantation:
Iḍi viḍi jiḍi khiḍi bhaḍi niḍi.
Ajika jitu kaṭi ajipaṇkujī.
Vasubhīśarīṇi alūhaṇi.

Vilade vimāli khu lu khu lu āśavakī gajimaha-gajim vakinaki-ku lu ku lu daphalau ju lu ju lu duṣadhamba du dhamba dumadhamba gunaye bilāye heṣu heṣu.
Hiri hiri miri miri tiri tiri.
Coulou coulou maohou maohou maohou maohou.

This Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī Sūtra:
if recited in the morning for one's own protection, one shall be secure throughout the day.
At evening, he spoke of self-protection so that the night might be peaceful and secure,
and he uttered this incantation:

Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ | Nāgari li | Tamba li li | Li-vimari li li | Hue-ye hue-ye | Viśa viśa | Dhubi-kubhi | Ira-mira | Igarāmi | Ili-mira | Ili-mi-tiri | Cili-mili-i-cili-hili | Tiri-mitiri | Suri-mitiri | Du-su-du-kura-cira | Ca-pala | Vira-ca | Icili-picili-cili | Nama āraghata | Araghara | Bhasathuti-pasamati-nānā | I shall now, for your sake, proclaim the Great Peacock King’s Heart Mantra.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*Iṭi miṭi tiḷi piḷi miṭi mili.
Tiṃmi sūdaṃ bhadra-pā.*
Śubhacirā-jīva-vijaya-mati-namo-buddhāya.

The *Dhāraṇī-viśeṣa-prabhāsa-mantra* is accomplished and auspicious.
Ānanda, this is called the Great Peacock King Mantra-heart.
Ānanda, this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī was spoken by Maitreya Bodhisattva in accordance with the truth.
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:

Śirili śiri śiri | bade dide śuśu | jivade lehe lehe lehe | arini | ṭṭe | śa | bale | śipe caracara | paṇi paṇi | bodhi bodhi | bodhi bodhi | sadhubodhibhāricarasiye | svāhā. Ānanda, this is the Great Peacock King Spell.
The Brahmā Sahāmpati, Lord of the Sahā World, in accordance with what was taught, then spoke this mantra:

*He-le he-le, ha-le-le-mi, ma-ri-ni, ba-gu-li ki-li, ki-li, ki-li ki-li, ki-li-ti, brahma-kaya kau-lan-da, kṣi-pi-tu-ha, bhu-lu bhu-lu bhu-lu bhu-lu, svāhā.* Ānanda, this is the Great Peacock King Mantra.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, in accordance with what had been said,
spoke this mantra:
Uccheḍe li | Śūrapati | Vīra | Vīra ||
Bhasira Bhasira Pate Svāhā. Ānanda, you have received these names of former seers and sages;
they bring ultimate auspiciousness, fulfillment of one's resolve, and accomplishment in incantations.
Constantly practicing asceticism while dwelling in mountain forests,
he possessed sovereign power and swift, miraculous transformations;
with the five supernatural faculties at his command, he traveled through the void as he willed.
I shall now declare their names:
they are known as the Great Sages of the Eight Liberations,
the Great Sage Vāma, the Great Sage Vāmadeva, and the Great Sage Pāli.
The Great Seer Śukra, the Great Seer Kṣema,
the Great Seer Āvarta, the Great Seer Kāśyapa,
the Great Seer Vṛddhakāśyapa, and the Great Seer Bhṛkuṭī.
The Great Sage Śrīghana, the Great Sage Īśvara,
the Great Sage named Mahānāman,
the Great Sage Mṛgaśiras, and the Great Sage Śālaka.
The Great Sage Dvayavipāka, the Great Sage Kṛṣṇa,
the Great Sage Śuci, the Great Sage Kṣānti,
the Great Sage Yaśas, and the Great Sage Nāva.
The Great Seer named Pigeon, the Great Seer named Horse,
the Great Seer named Snow, the Great Seer named Red-Eyed,
the Great Seer named Difficult Task, and the Great Seer named Vīryasāya.
The Great Seer named Armor, the Great Seer named Autumn,
the Great Seer named Venus, the Great Seer named Year,
the Great Seer Free from Strife, and the Great Seer Night-Walker.
The great seer named Jñāna, the great seer Aṅgulimāla,
the great seer Gandhadhara, the great seer Ekaśṛṅga,
the great seer Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, and the great seer Garga.
The great seer Dhananjaya, the great seer named Mūḍha,
the great seer Sīmāntaka, the great seer Kapphiṇa,
the great seer Gautama, and the great seer Rohitāśva.
The Great Seer Loma-harṣaṇa, the Great Seer A-nanda,
the Great Seer Keṇiya,
and others such as these were great seers who appeared earlier.
The four Vedas accomplish their purposes as desired;
they are well-practiced, majestic, swift, and possess great power,
performing all that is to be done— these too rely upon this Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Sūtra.
Protect [Name], granting him a lifespan of one hundred years and allowing him to see a hundred autumns.

Furthermore, by means of the Peacock King Mantra,
one shall protect such-and-such a person, causing them to live for a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.

The Sūtra on the Spell for Subduing Thieves Spoken by the Buddha. Homage to the Buddha. Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṃgha of Bhikṣus. Homage to all the Seven Buddhas of the Past. Homage to all the disciples of the Buddhas.
Homage to the Divine King Līcili! Having paid this homage and recited this incantation-sūtra, one’s wishes shall immediately be fulfilled.
To the north there is a mountain named Gandhamādana.
There is a spirit named Līcīlī who dwells in the mountains;

she has four disciples: Andhanī, Vemānī, Caṇḍanī, and Cauryamohinī. She causes thieves to forget their tasks, causes them to sit in haste, and causes them to plunder much. She causes thieves to be born in haste and establishes them as Caṇḍanīs. She causes thieves to become foolish. Thus, O Upalidrātimukha, she closes the teeth of the thieves.
When the thread is untied, may my protection, [O] So-and-so, be released.
May all those who are fierce, evil, harmful, or thieving be eliminated,
extinguished, and made to vanish.
When first preaching this *Caurasūtra*,
one should designate the twenty-ninth day as the *Kārttikī* festival;
one should light lamps and burn resin incense as the *Ībharaṇa*.
Seven lamps of scattered flowers:
for the sake of Hārītī, light seven lamps and recite this [mantra] seven times before Hārītī.
This is auspicious.
The King of the Ghost Children, who possesses merit and virtue, is named Li-li.
To honor him, one should light seven lamps, burn incense, and scatter flowers.

Abhiṇhāre dīrgha āluḍhavare śuddha-ujjure ālave.
Vārāṇasīkācārya-samāsamari.
Buddha-jivili-kauṭi-dharma-parikṣati-saṃgha-nirgūṣaṇe-vāśa-vāśa-śūda.
Mantadā kha mantadā kha yakṣada nāluda nāluda kauśalya akṣara.
Akṣayya-takṣayya-apalū-amanā.
I repeatedly urge the World-Honored One [to teach] this dhāraṇī mantra,
which has been spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of sixty-two Ganges Rivers.
Should there be anyone who violates or harms this Dharma-preacher, [they shall suffer the consequences].
This would constitute an offense against and a destruction of these Buddhas.
Regarding the dhāraṇī-spell spoken by Vīradatta: *satre mahāsatre ugre mukhe āre ārapathe nile nilete niletare icini vecini nilehe nile-apathe*. World-Honored One, this is the dhāraṇī-spell.
This is what has been spoken by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

This mantra was spoken by King Vaiśravaṇa: *Ari ṇali ṇuṇali ana-lu-na-li kuṇali*. This mantra was spoken by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra: *Akani gakani gauri gandhāri cāndāli mātaṅgi caṅguli bulūśani atti*. World-Honored One, this mantra was spoken by forty-two billion Buddhas.

The mantra spoken by the rākṣasī: *iti-li*, *iti-min*, *iti-li*, *ati-li*, *iti-li*, *min-li*, *min-li*, *min-li*, *min-li*, *min-li*, *lū-he*, *lū-he*, *lū-he*, *lū-he*, *ta-he*, *ta-he*, *dau-he*, *nau-he*. May it not disturb or confuse this Dharma-preacher; may it remain upon my head!
The head shall split into seven pieces like the branches of an *ari* tree.
This is the mantra from the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*,
the mantra spoken by Pāpīyān, the Māra King of the Sixth Heaven.
*Trakṣi trātratrakṣi lohale mahālohale āra carā tara svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One accepted this divine mantra, but did not accept the offerings.
The Sūtra on the Great Golden-Colored Peacock King Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha.
